answer: An optical attestation protocol curbs Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to physical tokens doped with disordered shale particles. Nodes authenticate by directing a coherent violet laser through the token, projecting a speckle pattern across a protective reef of verifiers. An attacker must fabricate distinct physical scattering keys per identity, incurring scarce nanolithography costs. However, adversaries can train neural models on observed responses to simulate the token digitally.
